1.why: All seven screenshots show a static, uncluttered layout with plain cards, no animations, carousels, or pop-up overlays.

2.why: Step headings, the green status banner, and the solid blue primary button stand out clearly, though the run-together step list items ('1. 1. Request2. 2. Confirm code') weaken visual hierarchy.

3.why: Each screen shows a single input plus one action button and a consistently placed 'Need help?' box, making the needed element easy to locate, apart from the cramped step breadcrumb.

4.why: The visible step tracker and per-step instructions reduce memory load, but the user must transcribe a 64-character token and a 6-digit code from a Logs panel and recall a 12-character password rule set.

5.why: No 'remember me' checkbox, autofill hint, password manager suggestion, or show-password toggle appears on any screen, including the sign-in step.

6.why: Nothing familiar is surfaced — no masked email confirmation, saved username, or account identifier is shown; only raw simulation log entries.

7.why: Text is short, in plain language, with generous line spacing and one- or two-sentence instructions per step (e.g., 'Use your new password to securely sign in.').

8.why: No error state is present in any of the seven screenshots, so the claim that error messages describe the problem and fix cannot be observed as true.

9.why: Requirements are stated in words ('at least 12 characters with uppercase, lowercase, number, and symbol') and token length is described, but no concrete sample input, placeholder, or worked example is shown.

10.why: Only a single password/code path exists at each step; no alternative sign-in options (code, biometric, face login) are presented, so choices are not shown as clear alternatives.

11.why: Each screen presents exactly one task and one primary button, so the user never faces multiple competing choices at once.

12.why: Every step opens with a green confirmation banner stating what happened and what is next (e.g., 'Code confirmed. Choose a new password, then complete one more safety check.') and ends with an 'All set' confirmation.

13.why: A persistent 'Need help?' card with pause/return and anti-phishing guidance plus a one-line hint under each step heading is present, though tips are identical rather than step-specific.

14.why: The step tracker and stated ability to pause, refresh and return imply retry is possible, but no explicit 'Back', 'Resend code', or 'Try again' control is visible on any screen.

15.why: All seven screens reuse the identical header, step tracker, card layout, banner style, button styling, and help/Logs placement.
